name: cdi_vf
description: C. difficile toxin panel: PaLoc TcdA/TcdB + binary toxin CDT subunits
note: Four markers cut from public INSDC records: strain 630 chromosome NC_009089.1 (tcdA WP_011860904.1, tcdB WP_009902069.1) and the CCUG 20309 CDT locus AF271719.1 (cdtA AAF81760.1, cdtB AAF81761.1). Sequences are byte-identical to the earlier locally-built panel; annotations re-derived from INSDC so no third-party database terms ride the distribution. Screen-only; no typing scheme.

references.citation: Sebaihia M, Wren BW, Mullany P, et al. The multidrug-resistant human pathogen Clostridium difficile has a highly mobile, mosaic genome. Nat Genet. 2006;38(7):779-786.
references.note: Strain 630, the genome behind the tcdA/tcdB records.

references.citation: Perelle S, Gibert M, Bourlioux P, Corthier G, Popoff MR. Production of a complete binary toxin (actin-specific ADP-ribosyltransferase) by Clostridium difficile CD196. Infect Immun. 1997;65(4):1402-1407.
references.note: The CDT locus (AF271719) behind the cdtA/cdtB records.

caveats: Toxin gene presence does not predict toxin production: tcdC/regulatory changes, PaLoc deletions and phase variation govern expression, and RT078/BI/NAP1 strains carry deletions in tcdC that this panel does not assess.
Binary toxin (CDT) genes are present in a minority of strains and can occur independently of the PaLoc; a CDT-negative PaLoc-positive strain still reads tcdA/tcdB positive.

tcdA/tcdB allele variation (including the tcdA-negative toxinotype XI and variant toxin B genes) may lower identity below default floors; read the identity column, not just presence, when variant toxinotypes matter.
